title: Watch: Mel Gibson Blasts California Gov. Newsom & LA Mayor Bass At Recall Event Following Deadly Fires
text:
Legendary Hollywood actor and director Mel Gibson joined the movement to recall California’s corrupt Democrat Governor Gavin Newsom, attending an event on Wednesday where he detailed how the governor and Democrat Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass have failed citizens.
Speaking about last month’s deadly California fires and the first responders who risked their lives to fight the blazes, Gibson said the emergency workers “did not let us down” but instead, “Governor Newsom and Karen Bass let us all down.”

The “Braveheart” star pointed out Californians aren’t properly taken care of by the government despite being subjected to the highest tax levels in the nation.
“Newsom, since he’s been in office, has brought us nothing but rampant crime, acute homelessness, horrendous inflation…” Gibson told the crowd, before noting Hollywood has been crushed as the former Mecca of filmmaking.
The actor detailed flying an entire film crew to Bulgaria for a shoot because it was cheaper than working in Los Angeles.
Gibson went on to discuss the Democrat agenda to rebuild L.A. into a “smart city” and compared the scheme to the Maui, Hawaii landgrab.
“Now Gavin has asked for $40 billion in federal dollars… Why would we trust him with that kind of money? You see, along with that money should come a federal investigation,” said the “Passion of Christ” director.
Attendees of the event cheered on Gibson and shouted out that Newsom and Bass are “criminals” as well as calling for a DOGE-style squad to clean up corruption and government waste in California.
“California deserves leadership that does more than acknowledge a problem, it deserves leaders that take real meaningful steps towards addressing these threats to our community. You deserve better, our firefighters deserve better and above all, the people who have lost everything deserve better,” he added.
The conservative actor’s message resonates with millions of Americans who are fed up with their state and local governments failing to uphold their constitutional oaths.
